messages:
emily: bringing up wildflower (hf/wildflower-1) embeddings on staging. initial qual looks off — clusters are weirdly tight, lots of near-duplicate neighbors. anyone else seeing this?
owen: yup saw it in the smoke run. ran recall@10 on wiki-mini holdout: beacon-v1 fp32 0.86 -> wildflower fp32 0.79 -> wildflower int8-perchannel 0.72. clustering UMAP shows a dense blob.
jia: can you paste a quick norm summary? could be layernorm/scale folding gone wrong during quant.
emily: norms: fp32 mean=1.02 std=0.12; int8-perchannel mean=0.14 std=0.03. also cosine sims across random pairs skewed to 0.97-0.999. seems like scale collapsed.
owen: interesting — we had a similar pattern when quantizing without calibrating the LN gain. i tried lowering knn cosine fallback threshold from 0.99 -> 0.985 in staging and the duplicate-neighbor symptom reduced. config diff:```yaml
knn:
  fallback_cosine_threshold: 0.985
  max_candidates: 256
```
deploy-bot: deployed wildflower-int8-perchannel -> staging at rev sha=3a7f9b (2025-09-14T18:04:12Z) :rocket:
jia: steps i propose: 1) run per-tensor vs per-channel calibration sweep, 2) check LN folding codepath (did we accidentally fold in a scale param?), 3) try fp16 quant fallback and dynamic scale clipping, 4) compute anisotropy and neighbor-distance histograms. i'll queue these tests.
emily: queued eval job: `python eval/recall.py --model wildflower --quant perchannel --holdout wiki-mini --k 10 --output /tmp/wf-int8.json` will paste numbers when done.
owen: also run a small synthetic noise sensitivity test: add gaussian noise (sigma 1e-3..1e-1) to input tokens and see embedding drift / recall degradation. that helps separate brittle postnorm vs representational collapse.
emily: quick diag output from /tmp/wf-int8.json after first run: """recall@1: 0.48
recall@5: 0.65
recall@10: 0.72
mean_norm: 0.142
std_norm: 0.031
pairwise_cosine_mean: 0.812
pairwise_cosine_90p: 0.995"""
jia: that 90p cosine ~0.995 is telling — long tail of very high-sim pairs. compute nearest-neighbor distance CDF and compare to beacon-v1 to see overlap. if mass concentrated near 1.0 we've got anisotropy/collapse.
owen: interim mitigation: enable prefix-KV cache bypass + the fallback cosine tweak; reduces user-visible dup hits while we fix quant.
emily: i'll open a small patch PR to adjust the export quant params (clamp range + calibrate with histogram bins) and a test harness to assert norm mean > 0.5 post-quant.
jia: for the calibration sweep, use both per-tensor and per-channel, and try bias-corrected min-max vs percentile clipping (99.9). log: `./scripts/quant_calib.sh wildflower --mode per-channel --clip 99.9`
emily: tagging @jia for followups, will post plots (umap, norm hist, nn-dist cdf) here. if recall@10 improves by >0.02 vs current int8 we’ll canary to dedicated. :thumbsup:
owen: one more thing — check tokenization / pooling differences vs beacon baseline. if pooling changed (mean vs first-token) that could shift norms systematically.
emily: good catch. current code uses mean pooling; beacon-v1 used L2-normed mean pooling + postnorm. adding that to checklist.
jia: summary of action items: [emily] run calibration variants + open PR; [owen] add synthetic noise sweep and knn fallback tuning; [jia] run LN folding audit and anisotropy metrics. aim for patch candidate EOD.
emily: ack, will update thread with PR link and final numbers.
